newsitem.title: USA: Triton confirms southern Bulan Field natgas.
newsitem.headline: Triton confirms southern Bulan Field natgas.

text.p: Triton Energy Ltd said Thursday one of the most prolific wells on Block A-18 of the Malaysia-Thailand Joint Development Area in the Gulf of Thailand confirmed the presence of natural gas in the southern portion of the Bulan Field.

The company said the Bulan-2 well encountered 207 feet of net pay in the shallow, normal-pressure and deep overpressure zones down to 8,424 feet, including 172 feet of natural gas pay and 35 feet of oil pay.
It was determined that only a limited flow-test program covering 60 feet of natural gas pay was necessary resulting in the best test results so far in a deep overpressure zone.

"Most of the gas pay in the Bulan-2 is located in a 108-foot-thick shallow reservoir sand. This sand was not tested, because it exhibited excellent log characteristics and was extensively flow tested in the Bulan-1 and in other wells in the area," Triton said.
On test, the Bulan-2 produced at a combined daily flow rate from only two intervals 30 million cubic feet of natural gas and 185 barrels of condensate.

The well was flow tested through choke sizes ranging from 1/4-inch to 3/4-inch. Flowing tubing pressure was 808 pounds per square inch, and the condensate ranged from 41 to 57 degrees API gravity. Electronic logs and fluid samples indicated two oil-bearing sands, which were not flow tested.
Bulan-2 was drilled in some 176 feet of water to a total depth of 9,160 feet about 4 kilometers, or 2.6 miles, south of Bulan-1, which was drilled earlier this year.

Triton has a 50 percent interest in Block A-18, while the rest is held by Petronas Carigali (JDA) Sdn.Bhd., an exploration and production subsidiary of Petronas, Malaysia's state oil company. -- Jim Brumm 212-859-1710.
